newsitem.title: USA: Court upholds Miami youth's sentence for killing.
newsitem.headline: Court upholds Miami youth's sentence for killing.

text.p: A Florida appeals court has upheld the life sentence given to a youth convicted two years ago in the killing of a German tourist in Miami, court officials said on Thursday.

In a ruling issued Wednesday, the state Third District Court of Appeals upheld a lower court's 1995 finding that Anthony Williams, then 21, ran over and killed Barbara Meller Jensen on April 2, 1993, while stealing her purse.
Prosecutors had said the German woman was lost in her rental car after arriving in the city with her mother and two young children when Williams and two other men spotted them.
They grabbed the purse, then crushed Jensen's head with their car as they drove away, prosecutors said.
Williams argued in his appeal that the trial judge was biased in favour of the prosecution, the state had not proved its case and the judge had refused to investigate possible juror misconduct.

The killing was one of a series of attacks on European tourists in the early 1990s that caused international outrage and helped shatter Miami's image as a vacation paradise, hurting Florida's $32 billion-a-year tourism industry.
